meta.description: Tuk Tuk — Mototaxis in your neighborhood. Request a ride, drive, or manage your fleet from the company panel.

passenger.title: Move around your city with Tuk Tuk Passenger
passenger.lead: The app to request mototaxi rides, follow your trip in real time, chat with the driver, and discover available riders in your area.

driver.title: Earn income with Tuk Tuk Driver
driver.lead: Go online, receive passenger requests near you, navigate the trip, and manage your daily rides. You can also join a fleet or cooperative.

fleet.title: Manage your fleet with the Tuk Tuk panel
fleet.lead: Create your company, choose a plan, invite drivers, control wallet and geo channels. The admin runs the cooperative; passengers and drivers use the real-time app.

passenger.benefits_lead: Tuk Tuk connects passengers with mototaxi drivers in your area, with tools designed to move fast and with confidence.
passenger.b1_text: Find active drivers near you and request rides whenever you need them, any time of day.
passenger.b2_text: Get a quote before you ride and know the trip value with no surprises. You pay what was agreed.
passenger.b3_text: Follow the route on the map, chat during the trip, and use in-app safety tools.
passenger.services_title: There's a Tuk Tuk for you
passenger.services_lead: As a passenger you request the ride, watch the live map, and coordinate pickup without friction.
passenger.s1_text: Request a mototaxi from your phone, set origin and destination, and get offers from nearby drivers.
passenger.s2_text: See the route, trip status, and location throughout the service.
passenger.s3_text: Coordinate pickup and drop-off details without leaving the app.
passenger.s4_text: Discover mototaxis and mobility supply in your neighborhood with geofences and area channels.
passenger.s5_text: Review past requests, completed statuses, and your recent activity.
passenger.s6_text: Know if your mototaxi is on the way, at the meeting point, or finishing the trip.
passenger.how_lead: Sign in with your Google account and start moving in minutes.
passenger.step1_text: Access with Google from the web or your device. No long forms.
passenger.step2_text: Set origin and destination, review the quote, and request a nearby mototaxi.
passenger.step3_text: Follow the map, chat, and close the trip when you arrive.
passenger.highlight_text: With geographic channels and geofences, Tuk Tuk shows active mototaxi supply in your area. Ideal for neighborhoods, urban zones, and local operators.
passenger.lost_text: From the app you can contact the driver or report an issue with your trip to get help.
passenger.cta_title: Want to drive with Tuk Tuk?
passenger.cta_text: Earn with your mototaxi, manage your schedule, and receive passenger requests near you. You can also run your own fleet from the company panel.

driver.benefits_lead: Go online, receive nearby requests, and manage your daily rides from your phone.
driver.b1_text: Get passenger requests in your area and decide when to accept based on your availability.
driver.b2_text: Turn availability on or off whenever you want. Work the hours that suit you.
driver.b3_text: Follow the route on the map, coordinate pickup by chat, and close the trip on arrival.
driver.services_lead: Everything you need to operate as a mototaxi driver on Tuk Tuk.
driver.s1_text: Go online to receive nearby passenger requests and pause when you're unavailable.
driver.s2_text: Review origin, destination, and estimated fare before accepting the ride.
driver.s3_text: Manage trip status: on the way, picking up passenger, and completed.
driver.s4_text: See the route and passenger location throughout the service.
driver.s5_text: Review completed trips and your recent daily activity.
driver.s6_text: Operate under a cooperative or transport company with access key and plan quotas.
driver.how_lead: Register in the panel, join a fleet or create yours, and open the app.
driver.step1_text: Enter the company / cooperative panel and create or join a Tuk Tuk organization.
driver.step2_text: The admin adds you as a driver. You open the Tuki app and sign in.
driver.step3_text: Go online, accept nearby rides, and earn in your neighborhood.
driver.highlight_title: You can also run your own fleet
driver.highlight_text: If you are a cooperative or mototaxi company, the fleet panel lets you create the company, manage drivers, plans, wallet, and geographic channels.
driver.cta_title: Want to drive with Tuk Tuk?
driver.cta_text: Earn with your mototaxi, manage your schedule, and receive passenger requests near you. You can also run your own fleet from the company panel.

fleet.benefits_lead: The admin runs the fleet from the dashboard: create the company, choose a plan, invite drivers, control wallet, and define geographic channels by area.
fleet.a1_text: Register name, phone, and responsible person. Get the access key for drivers and operations.
fleet.a2_text: Invite by email, assign the driver role, and control the driver cap according to your plan.
fleet.a3_text: Choose Starter, Growth, Business, or Enterprise. Pay with ePayco and consume trips by quota.
fleet.a4_text: Configure geofences and neighborhood channels to show mototaxi supply in each zone.
fleet.a5_text: Monitor completed trips, wallet balance, suggested company participation, and subscription validity.
fleet.a6_text: When you create the company, the selected plan quotas apply. Then renew with ePayco (30 days).
fleet.plans_title: Tuk Tuk plans for your fleet
fleet.plans_lead: Same structure as the admin dashboard: driver quotas, enabled trips, and suggested company participation. 5-day trial on signup; paid plans renew with ePayco.
fleet.how_lead: From company registration to trip matching in the driver and passenger apps.
fleet.step1_text: Enter the dashboard, register the cooperative, and choose the plan to start your trial.
fleet.step2_text: Add emails, share the access key, and control quotas according to the contracted plan.
fleet.step3_text: Monitor wallet and trips. When the trial ends, pay with ePayco to renew for 30 days.
fleet.cta_title: Manage your cooperative with Tuk Tuk
fleet.cta_text: The company panel gives you fleet, plans, wallet, and geo channel control. Your drivers and passengers use the Tuki app in real time.

payments.meta_description: P2L does not collect or hold the value of services. Payment happens between the parties. Platform cost is prepaid from the company balance; it is not charged again on each trip.
payments.title: P2L operating and payment model
payments.lead: P2L connects passengers, operators, and companies without holding trip money.
payments.problem: The issue is not the financial model, but the language. Terms like Settlement, ledger, driverShare, or take rate are technically correct, but they sound like internal accounting to an end user.
payments.names_note: Technical names stay in parentheses when they help development docs. The commercial term comes first.
payments.s1_img_alt: P2L costs, fares, transactions, and payment plans diagram
payments.s1_img_caption: The passenger pays the driver. P2L records the split: 80% operator, 20% company, 0% platform (the plan covers the cost).
payments.s1_p1: P2L does not receive or hold the money the passenger pays for the trip. The passenger pays the driver directly. The driver settles economically with the company, according to the operation’s rules. P2L only records that split; it does not transfer those amounts.
payments.s1_p2: The company buys a plan. That plan covers the platform cost: no extra percentage is charged at trip time.
payments.quote: P2L does not collect or hold the value of services performed between users, companies, and operators. Payment is made directly between the parties. P2L’s cost is paid in advance through the company balance. On each trip, P2L records and consumes the corresponding amount from that balance, but it does not receive money again from the passenger or the operator.
payments.s1_p3: P2L’s cost is a prepaid technology operating cost, not a commission charged again on each trip.
payments.s1_p4: These two sentences explain almost the entire financial model in plain language.
payments.split_driver_text: Trip share. Receives the passenger payment
payments.split_p2l_text: The plan covers the platform cost
payments.pax_l1: Sees the estimated value before requesting.
payments.pax_l2: Can join a bid when that option is enabled.
payments.pax_l4: Does not pay P2L for the trip. P2L does not receive that money.
payments.op_l1: Completes the trip and receives the passenger payment directly.
payments.op_l2: Records the final value and payment method in P2L.
payments.op_l3: Settles the company share economically (in the example, $4,000). P2L does not transfer that money.
payments.op_l4: Does not need a personal P2L balance. P2L does not charge the driver again for the trip.
payments.co_l2: Sets fares within the limits defined by P2L.
payments.co_l3: Buys a plan or tops up a P2L balance to use the infrastructure.
payments.co_l4: Reviews trips, shares, and prepaid-balance consumption.
payments.co_l5: The $4,000 in the example is the suggested company participation / gross income from the trip.
payments.pl_l1: Provides the technology that connects passengers, operators, and companies.
payments.pl_l2: Records trips and the economic split (80 / 20 / 0).
payments.pl_l3: The plan covers the platform cost. It does not charge an extra percentage at trip time.
payments.pl_l4: It does not charge the passenger or the operator again on each trip.
payments.pl_l5: Does not hold or settle trip money between the parties.
payments.vocab_note: The accounting term accrual is avoided in user-facing docs. Use 20% company participation / gross income instead.
payments.s4_p1: Technical docs use platformShare / platformAllocation, not fee. Commercially:
payments.s4_name: P2L service covered by the plan and prepaid balance
payments.s4_p2: The passenger pays the operator directly. The company defines or receives a share of the trip value. P2L already monetizes its service through the plan and the company’s prepaid balance: it does not charge again at trip time.
payments.s4_p3: The user does not need to see the limit clipping (clamp).
payments.s5_p1: The company defines or receives that share of the trip value. The passenger pays the operator. P2L does not present that percentage as an extra charge at trip time: its service is already covered by the plan and the prepaid balance.
payments.s6_p1: The plan covers the platform cost (0% on the trip). The company receives 20% of the value: $4,000. P2L does not charge the passenger or the operator again.
payments.s6_p2: The passenger hands $20,000 directly to the driver. P2L does not receive that $20,000.
payments.s6_l2: The driver does not physically receive $16,000.
payments.s6_p3: The $16,000 / $4,000 / $0 figures are the recorded economic split. P2L does not make three transfers. The driver settles with the company. P2L only records that $4,000 is the company share. The plan covers the platform cost.
payments.s6_p4: The plan covers the platform cost. On this trip that cost is 0% of the amount the passenger pays.
payments.s6_p5: The $4,000 is the suggested company participation / gross income from that trip. It is not a return on investment.
payments.s6_key: The plan covers P2L’s cost. On each trip P2L does not charge an extra percentage to the passenger or the operator.
payments.s6_r4: P2L platform usage (the plan covers the cost)
payments.s6_r7: P2L deducts from the prepaid balance
payments.s6_clarify_lead: P2L does not receive the $20,000 and does not resolve inside its platform:
payments.s6_c5: bank reconciliation of each passenger payment
payments.s7_p1: For an end user, wallet can sound like P2L holds passenger money. The commercial name is company P2L balance.
payments.s7_p2: The P2L balance is a prepaid amount the company uses for infrastructure. It is not passenger money and it is not the drivers’ balance. The plan covers the platform cost: in the example trip that cost is $0.
payments.s7_flow: Company → tops up P2L balance → P2L consumes platform cost from the balance → the company can keep operating.
payments.s8_l1: The passenger pays the driver directly.
payments.s8_l2: The driver records the final trip value.
payments.s8_l3: P2L records the split: operator, company, and prepaid platform cost.
payments.s8_l4: The driver settles the company’s share. P2L does not transfer that money.
payments.s8_l5: P2L consumes the trip’s platform cost from the prepaid balance. It does not charge the passenger or the operator again.
payments.s8_l6: The company tops up its balance when needed.
payments.tech_p1: Internally the trip split is recorded (RideSettlement) and the prepaid balance is consumed. The commercial field is platformShare / platformAllocation, not a fee charged again on the trip.
payments.tech_p2: There are two language layers: the top layer is clear to any business owner or user; the bottom layer is for the developer reading the system docs.
payments.cta_text: Top up your balance and operate with a clear split: 80% operator, 20% company, 0% platform (the plan covers the cost).
